<script id="scroll-bar-width-calculation">

    div.style.visibility = 'hidden'
    document.body.appendChild(div)

    document.body.removeChild(div)
    if(scrollbarWidth > 0){
        document.body.style.setProperty('--scrollbar-width', `${scrollbarWidth}px`)

</script>

Through ALMT, select alumni have the opportunity for peer-to-peer mentorship programs with the current scholarship beneficiaries. The proud ALMT team will prepare the next generation of the JEQ Foundation’s beneficiaries in Ghana.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">Seven (7) of our outstanding alumni have been selected to provide leadership and mentorship to existing scholarship recipients. They will also assist prospective scholarship applicants with information about the application process and post-award selection procedures.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The selected</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The selected alumni are:</p>
<ol class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Hildagard M. Musah</strong>: She will be responsible for the Western part of Ghana JEQ Foundation’s scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants. She will be assisted by Mabel Wiafe.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Abdul Rahman Lansah</strong>: He will be responsible for the northern part of scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Talita Anokye</strong>: She will be responsible for the Eastern and Brong regions of Ghana scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants. She will be assisted by Hayford Kankam Boadu.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Philip Nii Nortey</strong>: He will be responsible for the Ashanti region of Ghana JEQ Foundation’s scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Thomas Benson: </strong>He will be responsible for the Central region of Ghana scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Sarah Jalima:</strong> She will be responsible for the Greater region of Ghana scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants. She will be assisted by Rejoice B. Kojopeni.</p></li>
  <li class="wixui-rich-text__text"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><strong class="wixui-rich-text__text">Reagan Boulovi</strong>: Will be responsible for the Volta region of Ghana JEQ Foundation’s scholarship recipients and scholarship applicants.</p></li>

<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">Speaking at the ceremony, the Co-Founder/Co-President of the Foundation Prof. Joseph Emmanuel Quansah, said the Foundation was set up with the wife to support especially excellent but needy students in Ghana to ensure that they have at least a basic first degree.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">"Our hope and ultimate goal is to support as many Ghanaian students as possible in order to provide them the opportunity of having a good first degree. This will require resources and we would love to have corporate bodies to partner with the JEQ Foundation to provide academic and educational opportunities for students, especially Ghanaian students who are excellent and smart," he said.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The presentation was made by representatives of the Foundation in Ghana, with the attendance of some of the current and past recipients of the Foundation's scholarships.</p></div><!--/$--><!--$--><div id="comp-lnlygqk9__c7cfb402-a86e-42d1-8239-e90938510639" class="W4V2qg comp-lnlygqk9 comp-lnlygqk9__c7cfb402-a86e-42d1-8239-e90938510639 wixui-image text-align:center;"><span class="color_19 wixui-rich-text__text"><span style="font-family:montserrat,sans-serif;" class="wixui-rich-text__text"><span style="font-size:20px;" class="wixui-rich-text__text">The JEQ Foundation Award Laptops To Recipients</span></span></span></h2></div><!--/$--><!--$--><div id="comp-lnly9cs7__a06e8c0a-fc41-4f03-ae97-61cb121b7190" class="N8MGzv _v6ohL AWXfZq PO9MfV comp-lnly9cs7 comp-lnly9cs7__a06e8c0a-fc41-4f03-ae97-61cb121b7190 wixui-rich-text" data-testid="richTextElement"><p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The Joseph & Elizabeth Quansah (<a href="https://www.jequansahfoundation.org/" rel="noopener" target="_blank" class="wixui-rich-text__text">JEQ</a>) Foundation, a USA-based non-profit organisation, has urged brilliant but needy students across the country’s universities and colleges to take advantage of the Foundation’s scholarships to achieve academic excellence.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The Foundation, founded in 2019 in the USA to support Ghanaian students who excel academically but lack financial resources for tertiary education, provides tuition, residential scholarships, and laptops to selected students who have gained admission to undergraduate programs in public or private educational institutions.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">In addition to the financial support, the foundation provides academic advising, mentorship,<br class="wixui-rich-text__text">
and internship opportunities for scholarship recipients.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">Presenting laptop computers to some recipients of the JEQ Foundation scholarships in Accra based on their continued academic excellence and community service, Co-Founder and Co-President of the Foundation, Prof. Joseph Emmanuel Quansah, said the JEQ Foundation seeks to reach as many deserving students in Ghana as possible to help them on their path to higher education and realise their potential.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">He said it is therefore important that the scope of support is broadened to enable many young people to benefit from the initiative. Since its inception from 2019 to 2023, 43 students from various universities and colleges have received scholarship support worth about 85 thousand dollars. He appealed to corporate institutions to come on board, as this will help bridge the much-desired industry-academia gap.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">“We provide mentorship and internships to enable our scholars to have the needed industrial experiences before they complete their educational programmes,” he said.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">Touching on some challenges encountered over the years, Prof. Quansah mentioned the lack of awareness for many more students to access the opportunities the Foundation provides. This, he noted, is worrying, as he believes there are more brilliant but needy students across the country who must be assisted to further their education.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">He said, “there are very good students who lack the necessary resources to achieve educational excellence, so it is imperative that Ghanaian corporate institutions come on board to achieve this goal of assisting these people.”</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">The Ghana representative of the JEQ Foundation, Michael Nartey, explaining the criteria for selection, said students who apply for the scholarship after investigations are interviewed together with their parents or guardians to ascertain whether they qualify. Mr. Nartey commended the founders of the initiative and urged students to study hard to enable them to benefit.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">A student is expected to have results of at least 4As and 4Bs from WASSCE or be a Graduate with a GPA of 3.3 to qualify.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">“I run a school, and I know how difficult it is for some parents to pay fees, a situation which has led to many potentials going waste. It is therefore important that the JEQ foundation is aided to do more,” he added.</p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text"><br class="wixui-rich-text__text"></p>
<p class="font_8 wixui-rich-text__text">For her part, an aluminus and recipient of the JEQ Foundation, Hilvagard Maisha Musah from Takoradi Technical University, urged students to visit the foundation’s website to apply. She expressed appreciation to the founders and donors of the JEQ Foundation, as she is now working as a procurement officer after an internship with one of the companies she was linked up with through the assistance of the Foundation.</p></div><!--/$--><!--$--><div id="comp-lnlygqk9__a06e8c0a-fc41-4f03-ae97-61cb121b7190" class="W4V2qg comp-lnlygqk9 href=\"https:\/\/www.jequansahfoundation.org\/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\" class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\">JEQ<\/a>) Foundation, a USA-based non-profit organisation, has urged brilliant but needy students across the country’s universities and colleges to take advantage of the Foundation’s scholarships to achieve academic excellence.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\"><br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\"><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">The Foundation, founded in 2019 in the USA to support Ghanaian students who excel academically but lack financial resources for tertiary education, provides tuition, residential scholarships, and laptops to selected students who have gained admission to undergraduate programs in public or private educational institutions.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\"><br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\"><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">In addition to the financial support, the foundation provides academic advising, mentorship,<br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\">\nand internship opportunities for scholarship recipients.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">Presenting laptop computers to some recipients of the JEQ Foundation scholarships in Accra based on their continued academic excellence and community service, Co-Founder and Co-President of the Foundation, Prof. Joseph Emmanuel Quansah, said the JEQ Foundation seeks to reach as many deserving students in Ghana as possible to help them on their path to higher education and realise their potential.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">He said it is therefore important that the scope of support is broadened to enable many young people to benefit from the initiative. Since its inception from 2019 to 2023, 43 students from various universities and colleges have received scholarship support worth about 85 thousand dollars. He appealed to corporate institutions to come on board, as this will help bridge the much-desired industry-academia gap.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">“We provide mentorship and internships to enable our scholars to have the needed industrial experiences before they complete their educational programmes,” he said.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\"><br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\"><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">Touching on some challenges encountered over the years, Prof. Quansah mentioned the lack of awareness for many more students to access the opportunities the Foundation provides. This, he noted, is worrying, as he believes there are more brilliant but needy students across the country who must be assisted to further their education.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">He said, “there are very good students who lack the necessary resources to achieve educational excellence, so it is imperative that Ghanaian corporate institutions come on board to achieve this goal of assisting these people.”<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">The Ghana representative of the JEQ Foundation, Michael Nartey, explaining the criteria for selection, said students who apply for the scholarship after investigations are interviewed together with their parents or guardians to ascertain whether they qualify. Mr. Nartey commended the founders of the initiative and urged students to study hard to enable them to benefit.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\"><br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\"><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">A student is expected to have results of at least 4As and 4Bs from WASSCE or be a Graduate with a GPA of 3.3 to qualify.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">“I run a school, and I know how difficult it is for some parents to pay fees, a situation which has led to many potentials going waste. It is therefore important that the JEQ foundation is aided to do more,” he added.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\"><br class=\"wixui-rich-text__text\"><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8 wixui-rich-text__text\">For her part, an aluminus and recipient of the JEQ Foundation, Hilvagard Maisha Musah from Takoradi Technical University, urged students to visit the foundation’s website to apply. She expressed appreciation to the founders and donors of the JEQ Foundation, as she is now working as a procurement officer after an internship with one of the companies she was linked up with through the assistance of the Foundation.<\/p>"},"comp-lnlygqk9__a06e8c0a-fc41-4f03-ae97-61cb121b7190":{"height":683,"width":880,"fallbackTitle":"Abdul Lansah's class=\"font_8\"><br><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\">The Foundation, founded in 2019 in the USA to support Ghanaian students who excel academically but lack financial resources for tertiary education, class=\"font_8\"><br><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\">In addition to the financial support, the foundation provides academic advising, mentorship,<br>\nand internship opportunities for scholarship higher education and realise their potential.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\">He said it is therefore important that the scope of support is broadened to enable many young people to benefit from the initiative. He appealed to corporate institutions to come on board, as this will help bridge the much-desired industry-academia gap.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\">“We provide mentorship and internships to enable our scholars to have the needed industrial experiences before they complete their educational programmes,” he said.<\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\"><br><\/p>\n<p class=\"font_8\">Touching on some challenges encountered over the years, Prof. Quansah mentioned the lack of awareness for many more students to access the opportunities the Foundation provides.
